chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Yaḥyā ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Asbāṭ ibn Sālim narrated to me.
He said: I was in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), then a man from the people of Hīt came in to him and said to him, “May Allah set you aright.”
“What do you say concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘Surely in that are signs for the discerning’?”
He (عليه السلام) said: “We are the discerning ones, and the path is established among us.”

key_terms.آيَاتٍ: signs indicating divine truth and guidance
key_terms.الْمُتَوَسِّمُونَ: the ones identified in the hadith as possessing this discerning insight
key_terms.الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ: those who discern signs and perceive distinguishing marks
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ: the divine statement in the Quran

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones meant by “al-mutawassimīn” in the Quran according to Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic phrase about those who discern signs by identifying them with the Imams (عليهم السلام). It presents the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) as possessors of divinely granted insight and as the abiding locus of the path of guidance.
